statement: For supplied W, any dyadic row/column degree partition, block partition and acquired exact bilinear decomposition yield the shared-encoding, selected-output arithmetic upper bound (A) in RESULT.txt. The active tile count obeys q_ab <= min(m_ab, ceil(n_a/s)ceil(v_b/t), ceil(n_a/s)s delta_a, ceil(v_b/t)t epsilon_b).
interface: Dense X in Z^(N x D), dense Y in Z^(D x N), supplied W subset [N]^2; return exactly (XY)_ij for (i,j) in W. Degree classes and routing are acquired from W. Coefficient/decomposition acquisition and bit heights are separately charged.
proof: RESULT.txt, Degree-class and shared-output-local bound; proof of (A); degree-only tile count proof of (B).
falsifier: A tiled instance where an omitted rank term contributes to a requested coordinate, a requested pair is not output exactly once, or the active-tile count exceeds (B).
limitations: The bound is conditional on an acquired decomposition and its coefficient description. It does not imply that any choice makes the total subquadratic uniformly over masks.

statement: The direct selected-dot algorithm costs O(mD) field operations; m <= N min(Delta_L, Delta_R). At D=N^(1/4), m=O(N^(7/4-eta)) is sufficient for O(N^(2-eta)); a sufficient max-degree condition is min(Delta_L,Delta_R)=O(N^(3/4-eta)). These thresholds describe this algorithm, not all circuits.
interface: Same dense integer inputs and supplied mask as above. Entry height B and mask/output bits are charged separately in RESULT.txt.
proof: Each requested output uses D scalar products and D-1 additions; sum degrees equal m and are bounded by N times either maximum degree.
falsifier: A direct-operation count contradicting mD, or an incidence matrix with m>N min(Delta_L,Delta_R).
limitations: A large maximum degree can coexist with small m; degree maxima alone do not characterize the best general arithmetic circuit.

statement: L04 proves Omega(N^2) independently charged complete-block-cover cost for some legal masks, including masks with all row and column degrees Theta(N^(7/8)). N12 separately rules out subquadratic transfer through a subexponential-in-m-log-N library of fully evaluated masked kernels specialized only by coordinate copies/aliases and arbitrary output-linear decoding; its output-incidence test rejects specified recursive leaf-pruning kernels. Neither is a lower bound against arbitrary mask-dependent mixed-input arithmetic circuits.
interface: D=N^(1/4), mask size Theta(N^(15/8)) or floor(N^(15/8)); exact restricted models and quantifiers are stated in RESULT.txt under the L04 and N12 audits.
falsifier: For L04, exhibit a legal mask satisfying its simultaneous rectangle-density bound together with an independently charged complete-block cover of o(N^2). For N12, cover every balanced exact-size mask with a library meeting its stated kernel, entropy, and coordinate-copy assumptions, or show a concrete output-incidence profile below the stated rejection threshold for the cited fixture.
limitations: Immutable prior marks these claims source_derived_unreviewed. This leaf reconstructed the cited arguments but did not obtain external validation or prove novelty.

statement: No general deterministic O(N^(2-eta)) exact integer algorithm for every supplied W with D=N^(1/4), |W|<=N^(15/8) is established here, and no lower bound against general arithmetic circuits is established.
falsifier: A uniform exact mask-specialized circuit generator with total mask acquisition, preprocessing, shared encodings, arithmetic, output combinations, coefficient/field heights, and output writing all within O(N^(2-eta)) for all legal masks.
next_gate: Acquire final exact output maps for a genuinely mask-dependent mixed encoding; evaluate (A) uniformly over dyadic class/tile masks, apply N12 Psi(1/8) to each final kernel, and include the full bit/acquisition ledger.
